title: Surjectivity of the canonical special-chart map
statement: For arbitrary polynomial data d and maps c,cmod as in [def-weil-pbc-popescu-special-chart-map], suppose additionally that c(epsilon(X_i)) equals the original quotient generator x_i for every i. The canonical special-chart map [def-weil-pbc-popescu-special-chart-map] is surjective for every k. No Prepared hypothesis, conormal basis, smoothness, or normalization is assumed.

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 07CP, displayed calculation modulo pi and comparison of chart coefficients; read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CP on 2026-10-13.

proof.text: The canonical map contains all C0 coefficients and all free auxiliary variables in its range. Generalize polynomial compatibility to arbitrary R-algebras B and arbitrary maps q from the presentation polynomial ring, using MvPolynomial.algHom_ext on the original variables. Apply this proved generalization directly with B=T and q=F; hc supplies agreement on the generators after localization. Hence all original polynomials are in the range.

The image v of the coefficient inverse satisfies t*v=1. Every k-th defining chart equation, reduced modulo pi, says t*z_l=sum h_klj*z_j. Multiplying by v expresses every complementary auxiliary variable using the free ones and coefficient images. Polynomial induction puts every polynomial class in the range.

Surjectivity of the two quotient maps and ULift transport puts every D0 class in the range. IsLocalization.Away.surj expresses an arbitrary localized element z as a fraction z*t^n=x. Multiply by v^n to express it as x*v^n, still in the range.
